Deb Haaland

Democratic candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, New Mexico · Open seat

Former U.S. Secretary of the Interior

Deb Haaland, a citizen of the Pueblo of Laguna, served as U.S. Secretary of the Interior from 2021 to 2025 and represented New Mexico's 1st Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2019 to 2021. She won the Democratic nomination for governor in the June 2, 2026 primary, defeating Sam Bregman. She faces Republican Gregg Hull in the November 3, 2026 general election, and her running mate for lieutenant governor is Stephanie Garcia Richard.

Where Haaland stands

Taxes and affordability
Pledges to expand existing tax breaks for lower-income families. Opposes Republican Gregg Hull's plan to gradually phase out New Mexico's personal income tax.
Economy
Proposes a state Office of Small Business and faster permitting. Supports raising the minimum wage to a living wage and growing industries such as technology, film, aerospace and outdoor recreation.
Health care
Says she would work toward a public health care option, protect and expand Medicaid, ban medical debt from credit reports, and address provider shortages with rural residency programs and incentives.
Energy and climate
Supports a state commitment to net-zero emissions by 2050 and more renewable energy, community solar and battery storage. Proposes requiring data centers to supply their own energy infrastructure.
Data centers and water
Says data centers should have guardrails and communities should take part in siting decisions. Opposes industries using about one million gallons of water per day.
Immigration enforcement
Proposes limiting state and local cooperation with ICE, requiring agents to identify themselves and not wear masks, and barring ICE operations near schools, courthouses and health facilities.
Firearms
Supports new requirements for firearms dealers, safe-storage measures and gun-violence prevention offices. Says she will work to get illegal guns off New Mexico streets.
Abortion
Supports abortion access and reproductive rights, and has pledged to defend them as governor.
Education
Proposes earlier detection of reading problems, universal child care, bilingual instruction, statewide community schools, career pathways and more dual-credit opportunities.
Campaign finance and ethics
Proposes closing dark-money loopholes and strengthening lobbyist disclosure requirements.
